mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals weakening labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following a sustained GDPC1 decline, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within two months signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production challenges and higher costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO drops and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market downturn, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 3% quarter-over-quarter, it signals a strong economic rebound, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and GDPC1 on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals a strengthening housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
